what: Building a Character's step 4 ends: "Choose which hand is your main hand (see Hands)."
An open box after the building steps says starting gear and prices are not written yet: the GM and the player agree on a new character's weapons and armor.
The Hallmark Action line no longer says it doesn't need the Signature trait.

Distinct Choices now reads: each of your class's Attribute increases goes to a different Attribute; a species' and a class's increase can go to the same Attribute (the old example was replaced with the section).
foundry: Character creation in Foundry (the class's Attribute choices) must refuse the same Attribute twice from the class and allow a species and a class increase on one Attribute.

what: The parenthesis about every class letting you strike first or pray first is cut.
The Signature Modifier is the higher of the two Modifiers, with no "(if they are equal, choose one)".
Escalation Abilities is one line, "Each class's Apex is chosen at level 4 (see Escalation).", and keeps its open box.
The Advance card reads "You Advance your Speed. Once during it you can use Interact (see Advance)."; Chapter 3 keeps the rule.
foundry: The Advance card's text changed; its foundry sub ("move up to your Speed") no longer matches the text, so Foundry's Move button needs a new sub.

what: Chapter 1's Check row: one Attribute Modifier against a DC (a "Body Check"); a card can call for one inside an Action (Break Free, Tumble, Aid), and that roll is a Check, not an Attribute Action.
foundry: A Check called inside an Action (Break Free, Tumble, Aid) is a Check for every effect that names Checks, not an Attribute Action.

what: Chapter 1: a Tier of a Weapon Action that writes no [W] deals its damage as the weapon's damage too, with the weapon's type and subtype.
foundry: A Weapon Action's Tier with no [W] (Basic Attack's Tier 1 [V] 1d4!) deals the weapon's pool and subtype.

what: The rule that a Weapon Action takes Melee or Ranged from the weapon is only in Chapter 3 (Weapon Actions and Your Weapon) and the Weapon trait; it was cut from Basic Attack's Special, the Melee, Ranged, Firearm and Projectile traits, and Gear's Properties (and the Firearm property's last clause).
foundry: The Basic Attack card loses its Special line (its rules field, which Foundry shows as the card's description and Special line).

what: Charge stops on the first square from which the target is within the normal Range of the weapon you attack with.
foundry: Charge's movement must stop at the weapon's normal Range from the target, not at your Reach.

what: Crawl's 2 AP Version has its own Requirement line (Your Speed is 5 or higher) and Shake Off has a Save line and three Tier lines.
foundry: Crawl's 2 AP requirement is now a Version field (requirements) Foundry's cardgen and cardmodel don't read yet; Shake Off now has a vs (read as "roll" by vsKey) and tiers instead of effects, so its foundry sub "makes a Save" no longer matches and its automation must be redone.

what: Difficult Terrain: a movement of at least 1 square can always enter one square, whatever it costs, with an example (Mark Crawling into rubble while Prone, then Advancing with Speed 1).
foundry: Foundry's movement must let a 1-square movement (Crawl 1, Speed 1) enter one Difficult Terrain square.

what: Demoralize's Special: after you use it on a creature, whatever the Tier, you can't use it on that creature again this encounter.
foundry: Demoralize's Special text changed (Foundry's warning on an immune target already does this).

what: Evade's two Versions read "Evade 1." and "Evade half your Speed (rounded down)."
foundry: The Evade card's text changed.

what: Feint's Critical: until the end of your turn, the target can't use a Reaction for which you are the triggering creature.
foundry: Feint's Critical blocks only the target's Reactions triggered by you (Foundry blocks its Reactions against you).

what: Gear: Fists are used with the Fists Basic Action, and with a Weapon Action that isn't the Basic Attack.
foundry: The Basic Attack can't be made with Fists: Foundry's weapon choice for a Basic Attack must not offer Fists.

what: Haul and Relocate no longer say the target must remain within your Reach throughout the movement.
foundry: Foundry's cardgen keeps a Reposition within Reach only when the requirements say "remain within your Reach": Relocate's Reposition is now no longer held within Reach in Foundry.

what: Haul has a Special line: you can't choose your own square as the destination.
foundry: Haul's Pull can't end in the hauler's own square.

what: The Heal Basic Action is named Tend (card, Chapter 6's list in its alphabetical place, its open box); the word heal for removing damage is unchanged.
foundry: The Basic Action's name shown in Foundry becomes Tend (its key heal is unchanged).

what: Hide has a Special line: Senses don't change this roll: you don't need to perceive the targets.
foundry: Hide's roll ignores Senses modifiers.

what: Hide's Tiers 2 and 3: if the creature can't see you, you are Unsensed to it; otherwise you are Hidden to it.
Hide has no Requirement line.
foundry: Hide's requirements field is gone.

what: Interact's Special: while you are Hidden or Unsensed, a quiet use is Subtle if the GM agrees, and the GM can call for a Check; Chapter 7's Subtle says only "Interact can be: see its card."
foundry: Interact's Special text changed.

what: Lean: you count Line of Effect and Cover from one of your corners instead of the center of your square (Chapter 3's Leaning section is gone, B2-029).
foundry: Leaning in Foundry must count Line of Effect, not only cover, from the chosen corner.

what: Chapter 3's Leaning section is removed; the Lean card holds the whole rule (the ending on any movement, the cover steps, Total cover becoming High); the Glossary's Leaning row links to the card.

Point Out's Tiers 2 and 3: the ally perceives the target 1 step better: Unsensed becomes Hidden, whatever the reason; Hidden from Hide goes back to what its own senses give; never better than you perceive it.
foundry: Point Out improves Unsensed to Hidden whatever made the target Unsensed, not only Hide.

what: Point Out's Target: one creature you perceive (no Line of Effect needed).
foundry: Point Out needs no Line of Effect to its target.

what: Chapter 1: unless its card names another DC, an Action that rolls an Attribute against a creature rolls against that creature's DC of the same Attribute.
Regrip no longer says it doesn't have the Handle trait; Gear's Hands no longer has that parenthesis (the paragraph is now B2-076's pointer).
Release: you drop an object you hold, in your square, or take one hand off an object you hold with both hands (a Two-handed weapon is then held in one hand).
foundry: Release's text changed (its foundry sub still matches "drop an object").

what: Reload's Target: you, or one ally within Reach, holding a weapon that must be Reloaded; its Requirement line is cut.
foundry: Reload's target text changed and its requirements field is gone.

what: Reload has a Special above its roll: with a ranged weapon Reload is a [Ranged] Action, so its roll is Doomed while you are Engaged.
foundry: Reload with a ranged weapon is a [Ranged] Action: Doomed while Engaged.

what: Relocate no longer has the Strike trait (still At-will).
foundry: Relocate's traits lose strike: it no longer counts toward the At-will Strike count or the 3 Strikes a turn.

what: Seek's Tiers are printed once under a "1 or 2 AP" bar; the Target line keeps within 5 squares (1 AP) or 10 squares (2 AP).
foundry: Foundry's cardmodel must print Versions with identical lines once, as the book's cards.py now does (test t260 compares them).

what: Shove and Trip's Requirement: the target's SR is at most 1 higher than yours (as Haul and Relocate).
foundry: Shove and Trip's requirements text changed.

what: Sneak's movement doesn't trigger Reactions from creatures to which you are Hidden from Hide.
foundry: Sneak's no-Reaction rule applies only to creatures you are Hidden to from Hide.

what: Tumble: an enemy's space you pass this way costs 1 square.
foundry: Tumble's movement through enemies' spaces costs 1 square each (not Difficult Terrain).

what: Chapter 7 opens: an Action's traits are the words under its Flavor; each trait below has a rule of its own or is a word other rules and features refer to.
Divine, Fear, Focus and Magical share one entry: these traits have no rules of their own, and other rules and features refer to them; the Glossary's Magical row links to it.
Chapter 3's Areas says, after the Distance, that you need Line of Effect to the Point of Origin to place the area; the trait only points to Areas.
The Area trait: these Actions have an Area: they affect every creature in it and ignore Senses (see Areas and Senses).
An Action with more than one Attribute trait: you choose which of them to roll.
foundry: An Action with two Attribute traits (Trip, Relocate, Break Free, Tumble...) lets the player choose which to roll, not the higher automatically.

what: The sentence on a Vs. entry "the one used to roll" is cut from Chapter 7.
Firearm and Projectile no longer say the trait and the property have one name; the two Glossary rows say "A trait and a weapon property".

The Ranged trait: these Actions target creatures from a distance (how a range is written: Weapon Range; shooting next to an enemy: Ranged Combat While Engaged); a [Ranged, Weapon] Action needs a ranged weapon, or a Thrown weapon used thrown.

The Split trait is set aside: its Chapter 7 entry, Chapter 1's sentence and the Glossary's row (and its mentions in the Power roll and Weapon roll rows) are out of the book, kept in rules-src/set-aside/split-trait.md.
foundry: No card has Split; Foundry can keep or drop the trait key.

what: Strike: a Strike is an Action with the Strike trait: an attack aimed at a creature.
The Weapon trait no longer says a Weapon roll normally targets Armor or uses a DC when a rule calls for one.
Chapter 8 no longer says its conditions are in alphabetical order.
Chapter 8's opening points to Rounds and Durations for EoT or a number of rounds.
A condition with no duration lasts until the encounter ends unless its entry says how it ends; Prone adds "Prone lasts until you Stand" and "You give no cover to other creatures".
Blinded: your Sight perceives nothing and no Sight Sense helps; you perceive creatures only with your other senses; every square is Difficult Terrain for you; any Roll that needs sight is Doomed.
foundry: Blinded in Foundry: Sight and Sight Senses perceive nothing (other senses still do), every square is Difficult Terrain, sight rolls Doomed.

what: Chapter 2's Losing and Gaining AP adds: a card that wants the loss to carry over to the next turn writes Dazed (Dazed keeps its own line).
Chapter 1: an Empowered creature's 1d6! goes to the one creature it chose before the Saves (Chapter 8's rule wins).
foundry: Empowered on a Save Action: the die's target is chosen before the Saves and is lost if that creature takes no damage.

what: Empowered: the die deals one of the damages the Action deals, your choice before you roll it: its pool and its subtype.
foundry: Empowered's die takes a pool and subtype chosen from the Action's damages before it is rolled.

what: Grabbed ends when the holder lets go, when you leave its Reach, or when you Break Free (the holder going Down is the general source rule); Immobilized points to Break Free, the one Move Action you can use while Immobilized.
Immobilized: a Forced Movement or a Reposition that comes with no roll doesn't move you; the rest of the Action or effect happens.
foundry: Against an Immobilized creature, a rollless Forced Movement or Reposition fails but the rest of the Action still resolves (not disrupted).

what: Immobilized's roll needs to beat the Action DC of what Immobilized you, with no parenthesis repeating how that DC is made.
Imperiled: getting to safety takes no Action, so nothing can stop it; that turn you regain 1 AP less, as if Slowed 1 (adding to a Slowed value you have).
Lingering: Shake Off can end it, its Save against DC 13 or the DC the Lingering writes; the Tier results are on the card only; the rule on gaining Lingering again is unchanged.
Chapter 8 opens: "Some conditions are not on any card yet."
Vulnerable and Pressed no longer repeat that only the highest value applies (the chapter's opening says it).
Human: both choices are made when you build the character and can't be changed later.
foundry: Foundry's Human choices (Attributes, Health split) are locked after character creation.

what: Gear no longer says your class determines your Weapon Modifier.

"Pool" and "subtype" everywhere named: the weapon tables' column is Subtype; a weapon's damage has its own pool and subtype, written in its table; Chapter 4's instance has its own pool and subtype; Empowered says its pool and its subtype.
foundry: The weapon tables' column header (shown in any Foundry weapon table or tooltip) is Subtype.

what: Gear no longer says later weapons may deal Resolve damage.

Every placeholder weapon's Rung reads "Basic (placeholder)"; Light, Long, Thrown, Reload and Firearm say "(placeholder rule)"; the examples use only the four designed weapons (2[W] with a Hunting Bow, Steven with two Arming Swords, the Pike and thrown Dagger examples cut in Gear and Chapter 3, Reach 2 with a Longsword).
The paragraph on how weapon damage is balanced (melee more than ranged, the dice) is cut.
Two-handed: [Strike, Weapon] Actions with it held in one hand take 3 Banes, and the off-hand Banes too if that hand is your off hand.
foundry: A Two-handed weapon held in the off hand alone takes 3 + 2 Banes.

what: Gear's Hands: Actions with the Handle trait need a free hand; Release and Regrip change what your hands hold.
Barehanded keeps its words, with an open box: how a creature is disarmed, or a weapon broken, is not written yet.
Mastery no longer says a deeper weapon has fewer unlocks.
Fists have no Weapon Technique (no mention of Unarmed Talents).
An open box under Armor: Wards and their Ward values are not written yet; a character's Ward value is 0 for now.
foundry: A character's Ward value is 0 until Wards are written.
